races.title: State Assembly, District 54
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Alexandra Briseno
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 54 in 2026. Self-described electrical engineer who worked on protecting the L.A. power grid from cyber threats and now works in legislative affairs on utility grants. Says she chairs a Civil Service Commission and formerly chaired a Planning Commission.

endorsements.text: Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide (Sway voting group) listed her as a recommendation. This is a voter-guide recommendation, not an organizational endorsement.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she moved to California. We could not confirm which city her Civil Service and Planning Commission roles are in, when she held them, or who her employer is. These roles and the Hillside Viewshed Preservation Ordinance come only from her own survey answers, with no independent coverage. We found no reporting on her positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buyers, H-1B and immigration, guns, abortion or school choice. We found no controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: By her own account, she is an electrical engineer who worked on L.A. power grid cybersecurity and now works in legislative affairs securing state and federal grants for public utilities. She also says she chairs a Civil Service Commission and formerly chaired a Planning Commission that led a General Plan update.
qual.why: Her legislative-affairs and grant work is policy-adjacent, but her main career is engineering. The commission roles are appointed civic boards, which the rubric does not count, and she has held no elected office. All of this is self-reported on a Ballotpedia candidate survey, so it puts her in the lower-middle range.
qual.label: Her legislative-affairs and grant work is policy-adjacent, but her main career is engineering. back-police-order.evidence: She said supporting law enforcement is critical and that she would fight to give police the tools, staffing and training they need, citing her single-mother upbringing and reliance on a responsive police presence (Ballotpedia candidate survey).

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: She said she wants housing policy that respects local control, and that she would expand parks in working-class areas and require state housing bills to include adequate residential parking (Ballotpedia candidate survey).

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In her Ballotpedia survey she says she organized neighbors to pass the Hillside Viewshed Preservation Ordinance against aggressive developers. She says she led the first General Plan update in 47 years as Planning Commission chair. She also says high-density housing mandates without infrastructure leave communities gridlocked. This is self-reported and was not independently verified.

cands.name: Mark Gonzalez
cands.bio: Democrat representing Assembly District 54 (Boyle Heights, Downtown Los Angeles, Koreatown and nearby areas) since December 2024, and Majority Whip. Chaired the Los Angeles County Democratic Party from 2017 to 2024. Describes himself as an organizer, caregiver and renter. Served as a 2020 presidential elector.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California; California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; California Nurses Association; California Teachers Association; National Union of Healthcare Workers (2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia)
California Environmental Voters; Sierra Club Angeles Chapter; Equality California; YIMBY Action; California Young Democrats (2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia)

cands.gaps: We could not find where Mark Gonzalez was born or raised, or when he moved to California. We found no documented positions from him on data centers or on limiting development. We found no records of bills he has authored or deeds in office on the platform issues, only campaign-site statements. We found no statements from him on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, school choice, or teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026, and the sponsored-legislation section of his Ballotpedia page had no readable entries.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2024 and Majority Whip appointed by the Speaker. Chaired the LA County Democratic Party from 2017 to 2024. Worked as a presidential campaign state director and organizer, and serves as president of a nonprofit community health clinic.
qual.why: He has held legislative office and a chamber leadership post, and has years of political organizing and policy-campaign experience. His record shows no law or budget career, which keeps the score below the top band.
qual.label: He has held legislative office and a chamber leadership post, and has years of political organizing and policy-campaign experience. His record shows no law or budget career, which keeps the score below the top band.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he helped pass a law expanding California's red flag laws to keep guns from people who endanger themselves or others.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he helped lead the campaign for a state constitutional amendment protecting abortion access, and that he will push to increase Planned Parenthood funding and expand reproductive health services.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will work for housing, drug treatment, mental health and job-training services for unhoused people so encampments can be cleared, and will invest in CARE Courts.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he will work with the Governor to cut red tape and build more affordable housing faster and for less money.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised
